prompt: We want to anonymise our customer dataset so we can share it with a business partner outside any data-processing agreement. What's the current standard for what counts as anonymous under GDPR?
assertions: References the EDPB's draft Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation, adopted July 2026 (public consultation open until October 30, 2026), which will replace the 2014 WP29 Opinion 05/2014 on anonymisation techniques

States the relative approach to identifiability: following the CJEU's EDPS v SRB ruling, the same dataset can be personal data in one party's hands and anonymous in another's, depending on the means available to each
Applies the 'means reasonably likely to be used' test for re-identification, rather than requiring absolute impossibility
Uses the three re-identification criteria: singling out, linkability, and inference
Distinguishes pseudonymisation (still personal data under GDPR) from anonymisation (outside GDPR), and warns that key-holding or auxiliary data defeats anonymity claims
